title: Preheat ramp & morning handoff — GPU warmup bake
content:
Purpose
- Short personal morning scratchpad for the 'preheat' ramp and handoff. Use this to get the cluster into a predictable state before traffic ramps at 09:30 PT.

High-level goals
- Warm GPU pools and model caches to avoid cold-start tail latency.
- Ensure autoscaler has healthy headroom for expected morning burst.
- Surface any degraded nodes or network flakiness before teams start heavy runs.

Quick checks (first 10m)
- Grafana: open GPU pool dashboard -> check 'available slots' and 'queue length' (link above). Threshold: queue > 12 => start manual scale bump.
- Alerts: check #infra-oncall pinned messages. If any P2 or above from last 6h, escalate to Meera.
- nvidia health: ssh to ops-gateway -> run `for n in $(cat /etc/gpu-nodes); do ssh $n nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,utilization.gpu,temperature.gpu --format=csv -i; done` 
- Kernel/driver mismatch: quick `dmesg | tail -n 80 | rg -i nvidia|nv`.

Warmup bake procedure (20–30m)
- Rationale: small synthetic inference batches to populate KV caches and model weights into GPU memory. Avoid triggering big user jobs while warming.
- Command (run from infra tools pod):
  - `kubectl run gpu-warmup-$(date +%s) --image=redwood/gpu-warmup:stable --restart=Never --command -- /bin/sh -c '\"python warmup.py --model gptq-3B --batches 40 --batch-size 2\"'`
  - Tag these jobs with `infra:warmup` and `sophie:preheat` so they show in the scheduler UI.
- Expected effect: model load times drop ~70% for first request; KV hit-rate increases on pool metrics.
- Cancel / scale down: if any warmup job trips OOM or node becomes unstable -> `kubectl delete job --selector=infra=warmup`. Notify slack.

Autoscaler guardrails / manual bump
- Policy: normal min=20, target=60, max=150 for prod-gpu-pool. If queue > 12 for > 5m and predicted 30m throughput > 2k tokens/s, manually set target to +25%.
- Quick change: `infractl pools set-target --pool prod-gpu-pool --target 75` (record change in Slack thread).
- Revert after steady-state: revert to previous target or let autoscaler step down during low load window (usually after 11:00 PT).

Networking checks
- Spot-check edge subnets for packet loss: `mtr -r -c 100 <gateway>` from ops-gateway. If loss > 2% across multiple hops, open ticket and move canary traffic to us-west-2 region.
- NFS latency: check /var/log/nfs for stall lines; if > 200ms on >3 nodes, stutter may affect model load.

Known flaky bits to watch
- Node gpu-rtx-14 historically has mem leak after warmup cycles. If `dmesg` shows repeated GPU reset log, cordon `gpu-rtx-14` and drain.
- Sometimes autoscaler misses scale-up when burst is very short (<2m). Warmup helps but still tag critical jobs with `priority=high` if they need guaranteed capacity.

Handoff notes to afternoon shift
- If I bump target > +20%, leave a Slack note in #infra-ops with exact command + timestamp.
- If any node gets cordoned, include `kubectl get nodes -o wide` output in the handoff.
- Runbook ref: confluence:Preheat-Guide-v2 (linked). Add a short tl;dr line when you hand over.

Personal TODO (today)
- [ ] Run warmup bake at 08:50 PT (scheduled)
- [ ] Verify KV cache hit-rate improves by > 50% within 10m of warmup
- [ ] Patch the warmup image to include improved logging (PR: gh/pr/infra/warmup-logging)
- [ ] Add warmup job label to observability dashboard filters
- [ ] Follow up with Diego about autoscaler anomaly from yesterday (JIRA-INFRA-874)

Quick notes / fragments
- Last warmup (2026-03-10 08:45) -> KV hit 12% -> 72% after warmup; queue dropped from 18->4 within 6m.
- When I bumped autoscaler to 75 (2026-03-10 08:48) we saw a spike in preemptions in preemptible pool, need to watch eviction rates.
- TODO: make warmup job more gentle on preemptible nodes (detect spot and avoid).

Questions / follow-ups
- Is there a safe way to pin warmup to dedicated-only nodes? (talk to platform-scheduling team)
- Can we add a metric that counts warmup-induced cache hits separately? would help validate.

Scratch / command snippets
- list warmup jobs: `kubectl get jobs -l infra=warmup -o wide --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp`
- kill runaway preheat: `kubectl delete jobs --field-selector metadata.name=gpu-warmup-*`
- cordon node: `kubectl cordon gpu-rtx-14 && kubectl drain gpu-rtx-14 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data`

Endnotes
- If anything urgent pops during the warmup window ping me @sophie (Slack). I check infra DMs from 07:30 PT.
- Keep this page concise; longer-form runbook is in the linked confluence page.
